title: Sallie: The House on North 2nd
summary: In the early 1900s a little girl was carried into a doctor's front-room office in Atchison, Kansas, with a burning pain in her side, and she never came out. In 1993 a young couple moved into the same house and had a baby there. Toys gathered in circles around the crib, pictures turned upside down, burners lit themselves and the father woke with scratches in rows of three. They fled before the baby's first birthday. The house has kept two things ever since: the girl everyone calls Sallie, and something else that answers when people say her name.

characters.name: Mrs. Ilse Vantreese

art.description: small elderly woman with a white braid, quilted pink housecoat under a man's brown canvas parka, rubber boots, a heavy silver flashlight held to her chest
idle: standing still, flashlight held to her chest

dialogue: Lord, look at you. Wren Corwin. You were this big. I carried you out that door myself.
I've lived across the street since '71. Your folks, Ray and Dana, nice kids. They didn't last two years in there.
Your mama'd find the stuffed animals circled up on the nursery floor round your crib. Every morning. Nobody'd touched them.
Pictures turned upside down on their nails. That stove lighting itself in the night, and Ray swearing the knobs were off.
And your daddy's arms. Scratches, honey. Always three lines, like fingers. Got worse every week.
Night they left in '94 he loaded the car bleeding through his shirt. I held you in your yellow blanket till Dana could take you.
Here's the key. And listen: there's always a woman sitting in the front room. Tour folks see her. Be polite to her.
afterwards: I've told you all I know, honey. I'll be right here with the flashlight.

examine: A brass placard on a stand: 'A. VAIL, M.D. – SURGERY.' The frosted door beside it is locked tight.
Through the frosted glass, a sick green glow and the dim shape of a tall, narrow table.
The air at the keyhole smells sweet and chemical. Ether.
afterwards: Locked. The green glow breathes behind the glass.

characters.name: Nell Tolliver

art.description: ghost of a thin young mother from the early 1900s seated on a bench, high-collared white shirtwaist, long dark wool skirt, hair pinned up and coming loose, a small red child's coat folded in her lap, faint grey-blue translucence, red-rimmed eyes staring ahead
idle: sitting upright with hands folded on the red coat, staring straight ahead

dialogue: Oh. Are you here for the doctor too? He said it would only be a little while. He said to wait here.
My Sallie. Six years old. A pain low in her right side, burning, she couldn't stand up straight.
He took her straight through that frosted door. Said he had another patient coming and there wasn't time.
I heard the ether bottle clink. And then, too soon, so much too soon, I heard her screaming my name.
Then it went quiet. And the door never opened again.
She's upstairs now, in the nursery, with the toys. She won't come down to me.
The last man who lived here locked that room. I watched him hide the key in the breadbox on the kitchen counter, through the west door.
Be careful on the stairs, miss. Something else goes up and down them, and it isn't her.
afterwards: I've told you all I know. I have to wait here. He said to wait.

They're darkest out here, away from the stove, and they fade as they reach it. The fires started in the wall and spread toward the burner.
Three thin lines are scratched through the soot, a finger's width apart.
afterwards: Three lines through the soot. Always three.

examine: Ray Corwin's notebook, spotted with coffee rings. The entries run from 1993 into 1994.
'Burner on again. Knobs OFF.' 'Toys in a circle round the crib. Dana says she didn't.'
'Woke up with scratches. Three lines. Always three.'
Last entry, pressed hard: 'Locked the nursery. Key in the breadbox. Cellar key is gone off its nail. We leave Friday.'
afterwards: 'Key in the breadbox.' 'We leave Friday.' My father's handwriting, shaking.

characters.name: Sallie

art.description: translucent grey-blue ghost of a six-year-old girl from the early 1900s, plain white cotton nightgown, bare feet, dark hair in a loose braid, pale round face with large dark eyes, one hand pressed to her right side
idle: sitting cross-legged on the floor, one hand pressed to her right side, looking up

dialogue: You got big. I watched you when you were little.
I put the animals out every night, all the way round your crib. It won't cross them. So it couldn't get close.
I didn't scratch your papa. I wouldn't. That was the Other One.
It came after me. It tells people it's me, because nobody wrote my real name down.
I took the key off its nail in the kitchen so your papa couldn't go down there again.
The Other One lives down in the cellar with the doctor's old things. His key to the room with the table is in his cabinet down there.
Here. Be quick. It's very slow. But it doesn't ever stop.
afterwards: I told you all I know. I have to stay with the animals.

Rows of rusted scalpels and clamps lie on rotted green felt. A cracked ether cone sits on the top shelf.
Three long scratches cross the glass from the outside, as if something wanted in.
The bottom drawer sticks, then gives. A brass key on a cardboard tag slides out: 'Surgery — A.V.'

A deep, flat voice: 'Sallie. Sallie. Sallie.' Three times. It's trying to sound like a little girl, and it gets it wrong.
afterwards: The tape has run out. Only hiss now.

examine: The table is narrow and cold. Its leather straps are cracked, sized for a grown man.
Every buckle is pulled to its very last hole, as small as it will go.
Caught in one buckle is a child's red hair ribbon, still tied in a bow.

examine: A brown glass bottle, still uncorked. The label reads: 'ETHER, for anaesthesia. Allow four minutes.'
Beside it, a wire-and-gauze mask, the gauze yellowed stiff.
The bottle is nearly full. Barely any of it was used.
afterwards: The ether bottle is nearly full. Four minutes, the label says.

props.name: instrument stand with Dr. Vail's open leather daybook

parts.art: open leather-bound daybook with shaky handwritten ink entry, 'Not reported' underlined twice in the margin
white enamel kidney dish holding rusted scalpels and clamps

examine: The daybook is open. The entry is in a shaking hand.
'Female child, aged six, brought by mother. Pain right side; appendix. Second patient waiting.'
'Began before the ether had taken. Child woke. Lost her at ten past four.'
'Mother gave the name Sarah, called Sallie.'
In the margin, underlined twice: 'Not reported.'
No certificate. No record. A name nobody wrote down, so something else could wear it.
You say it aloud, here where it was hidden: Sarah. Sallie. Upstairs, softly, the toys tip over. Below, the scratching stops.
afterwards: Sarah, called Sallie. Ten past four. You've said her name. Tonight, the house is quiet.

characters.name: Dr. Amos Vail

art.description: translucent grey-blue ghost of a tall gaunt early-1900s physician, grey mutton-chop whiskers, wire spectacles, starched collar, black waistcoat under a long white surgeon's apron, sleeves rolled, hands red and raw, half-turned away scrubbing his hands
idle: scrubbing his hands together, head bowed
wringing his raw hands, glancing over his shoulder

dialogue: It was an emergency. Appendix. There was no time. Do you understand? There was another patient.
The ether wants four minutes. Four. I gave it two. Barely two. I thought my hands were quick enough.
She woke. On the table. She called for her mother.
I told the mother nothing. I closed the door. I wrote it once, in my daybook, and I never spoke of it again.
No certificate. No report. As if she'd never been born at all.
And something came into this house that liked a secret like that.
A name nobody writes down is a name anything can wear.
It's in the daybook. On the stand. Read it. I can't.
afterwards: I've told you all I know. I have to finish washing.

objectives.text: Talk to Mrs. Vantreese at the front gate of the Sallie House
Unlock the front door and speak to the woman in the waiting room
Search the breadbox in the kitchen, west of the waiting room
Climb the stairs in the east stair hall and unlock the nursery
Unlock the cellar door in the kitchen and find the doctor's cabinet
Open the frosted surgery door in the waiting room
Read Dr. Vail's daybook on the instrument stand
